newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa aims to complete EU trade talks by end-97.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa aims to complete EU trade talks by end-97.

text.p: South Africa said on Monday it had presented a fresh offer in bilateral trade talks with the European Union during discussions in Brussels last week and hoped to complete detailed negotiations by the end of the year.
A ministerial meeting will be held in Brussels on July 18.
"South Africa presented a supplementary offer in support of its earlier position," the Department of Foreign Affairs said in a statement following the 12th round of technical discussions.
"The offer provides for both the framework and the time schedule for the proposed dismantling of tariffs with the view to complete the detailed negotiations by the end of 1997."
The department said the offer committed Pretoria to free trade while providing for a mechanism to address the "severe adjustment" which would be faced by certain industry sectors.

No details of the offer were provided but Business Day newspaper quoted sources close to the talks saying South Africa had proposed an ambitious trade pact suggesting that all trade exchanges be freed within 12 years.
The June 19-20 discussions appear to have given new impetus to lengthy South African-EU trade negotations.
Earlier this year Pretoria was given qualified membership of the Lome Convention, the cooperation agreement between the EU and 70 African, Caribbean and Pacific countries.
Now Pretoria and Brussels are working to hammer out a separate Free Trade Area.
The South African government said both sides had underlined their firm intention to negotiate a free trade pact which was fully compatible with World Trade Organisation obligations.

"The Free Trade Area will be based on the principles of differentiation and asymmetry and will be designed in a way which is conducive to the process of trade cooperation and integration in the SADC region," the department said.
Pretoria is concerned to ensure that a bilateral trade deal with Brussels does not damage the economies of fellow members of the 12-member South African Development Community.
